questions.prompt: While the ducks were swimming in the pond, the farmer was resting.
questions.answer: Dum anatēs in stāgnō natābant, agricola requiēscēbat.

questions.prompt: The fleeing enemy will abandon the city walls tomorrow.
questions.answer: Hostēs fugientēs crās moenia relinquent.

questions.prompt: Let us relax our minds, so that we may endure long labors.
questions.answer: Animōs relaxēmus, ut longōs labōrēs ferāmus.

questions.prompt: The teacher was speaking so that all the students might understand.
questions.answer: Magister loquēbātur ut omnēs discipulī intellegerent.

questions.prompt: The city, having been captured by the enemy, was destroyed.
questions.answer: Urbs ab hostibus capta dēlēta est.

questions.prompt: The gifts sent by the king will have been received by the citizens.
questions.answer: Dōna ā rēge missa ā cīvibus accepta erunt.

questions.prompt: The sausage, cooked with great care, was praised by the guests.
questions.answer: Lucānica magnā cūrā cocta ab hospitibus laudāta est.

questions.prompt: The general reported that the enemy were making for the camp.
questions.answer: Dux hostēs castra petere nūntiāvit.

questions.prompt: I believe that the merchants have crossed the vast sea.
questions.answer: Mercātōrēs vāstum mare trānsīsse crēdō.

questions.prompt: She promised that she would return before winter.
questions.answer: Sē ante hiemem reditūram esse prōmīsit.

questions.prompt: We knew that the city would be defended by brave men.
questions.answer: Urbem ā fortibus virīs dēfēnsum īrī sciēbāmus.

questions.prompt: The daughter, about to depart, embraced her weeping mother.
questions.answer: Fīlia discessūra flentem mātrem complexa est.

questions.prompt: By reading good books we increase our wisdom.
questions.answer: Bonōs librōs legendō sapientiam nostram augēmus.

questions.prompt: The bridge must be built by the soldiers within three days.
questions.answer: Pōns ā mīlitibus tribus diēbus faciendus est.

questions.prompt: The dying leader, still hoping for victory, encouraged his men.
questions.answer: Dux moriēns, adhūc victōriam spērāns, suōs hortātus est.

questions.prompt: The envoys came to seek peace from the Romans.
questions.answer: Lēgātī pācem ā Rōmānīs petītum vēnērunt.

questions.prompt: This story is wonderful to tell but hard to believe.
questions.answer: Haec fābula mīrābilis dictū sed difficilis crēditū est.

questions.prompt: Endure the bitterness of the present, and do not be forgetful of your friends.
questions.answer: Praesentis amāritūdinem tolerā, nēve amīcōrum immemor sīs.

questions.prompt: If you had listened to me, you would not have lost the way.
questions.answer: Sī mē audīvissēs, viam nōn āmīsissēs.

questions.prompt: The soldiers, having conquered the enemy, returned to the ancient city.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs, hostibus victīs, ad urbem antīquam revertērunt.

questions.prompt: The venerable old man said that he had kept watch the whole night.
questions.answer: Senex venerābilis dīxit sē tōtam noctem vigilāvisse.

questions.prompt: The city will be destroyed by the fire raging through the narrow streets.
questions.answer: Urbs igne per angustās viās saeviente dēlēbitur.

questions.prompt: When the poet had recited his verses, the whole crowd applauded eagerly.
questions.answer: Cum poēta versūs recitāvisset, tōta turba avidē plausit.

questions.prompt: About to set out at dawn, the merchant entrusted his money to a friend.
questions.answer: Prīmā lūce profectūrus, mercātor pecūniam amīcō crēdidit.

questions.prompt: The maidservant, keeping watch, heard the thieves approaching the silent house.
questions.answer: Ancilla vigilāns fūrēs domuī silentī appropinquāre audīvit.

questions.prompt: When the guest had watered the thirsty horses, he set out through the dark forest.
questions.answer: Cum hospes equōs sitientēs rigāvisset, per silvam obscūram profectus est.

questions.prompt: The witness had bound the captive with chains before the judge arrived.
questions.answer: Testis captīvum catēnīs obligāverat priusquam iūdex advēnit.

questions.prompt: By dawn the soldiers will have surrounded the walls of the hostile city.
questions.answer: Prīmā lūce mīlitēs moenia urbis hostīlis cīnxerint.

questions.prompt: The parsimonious old man had hidden his gold in a hollow tree.
questions.answer: Senex parcus aurum suum in arbore cavā abdiderat.

questions.prompt: The gifts, brought back by the returning envoys, delighted the king.
questions.answer: Dōna ā lēgātīs redeuntibus relāta rēgem dēlectāvērunt.

questions.prompt: This deed is dreadful to see and dreadful to relate.
questions.answer: Hoc facinus dīrum vīsū et dīrum dictū est.

questions.prompt: The general promised that the bridge would be built within a few days.
questions.answer: Dux pontem paucīs diēbus aedificātum īrī prōmīsit.

questions.prompt: About to cross the sea, the merchants bound the ropes to the mast.
questions.answer: Pelagus trānsitūrī mercātōrēs fūnēs ad mālum nexuērunt.
